title: GitHub - Ephemeral-AI-Lab/layerfs: Ephemeral Workspaces, durable shared history. LayerFS gives every agent a complete, writable filesystem Workspace over shared committed history, without copying the base. Agents work in parallel, commit what changed as deduplicated checkpoints, then branch, rewind or merge. Try it with LayerFS × DSH.
html:
Ephemeral Workspaces. Durable Shared History.

LayerFS is the substrate under your agents. Each one mounts a complete, writable Workspace over shared committed history, does its work, commits what it changed, and goes away.

Get started · Website · Docs · Benchmarks · Video · LayerFS × DSH · Community

layerfs-v1.0.0-release-720p.mp4

Status: LayerFS 1.0.0, the first official release after the 0.1.x Developer Previews, released as source. The results below ran on 

main
at 
e5c7aaae05
. The Store runs in its Disposable profile only, with no crash or power-loss durability: use LayerFS for agent work and its history, not as the only copy of data you cannot rebuild.

LayerFS runs today through LayerFS × DSH, the 

dsh-layerfs
plugin for DeepSeek Harness. Agents in a dsh session fork Branches, test them in Sandboxes, merge and publish, and the Work and History tabs show every agent's Branch, live.

01 · Ephemeral Computing

Compute exists only while a command runs.

02 · Decentralized Agents

Agents on different computers share one serverless Store.

03 · Multiagent Coordination

One project, many Branches. One Branch, many agents.

04 · Recursive Filesystem

Fork recursively any Commit, at any depth.

05 · Ultra Storage Optimization

157 snapshots of a real project in 100 MB, 19.9× smaller than Btrfs + zstd.

06 · Instant Bootstrap

Dependencies come with every mount. No time lost reinstalling.

And underneath them

Supporting idea In one line
07 · Auto Checkpoints Every step an agent takes is a checkpoint to return to.
08 · Append-only Objects Saved objects are never rewritten. The Store only grows.
09 · Conflict Rules (
.lww
)		 Name the files that should never conflict. The newest edit wins.
10 · Big File, Small Edit An edit costs the size of the edit, not the size of the file.

Agents fork Branches, work in Workspaces inside Sandboxes, commit, merge and publish to 

main
. The history grows as they go.

Every suite ran once on 

main
at 
e5c7aaae05
through the JavaScript SDK. Each row links to its method, environment and receipts.

Suite What it measures LayerFS 1.0.0
fs-bench Cloudflare Computer's own twelve-scenario filesystem benchmark, unchanged, same image5.20 s vs 8.88 s, 1.71× faster; faster in 10 of 12 scenarios
dsh-dedup A real project's history, 157 snapshots (4.94 GB of trees), kept as mountable Commits100.1 MB vs 1,994.6 MB, 19.9× smaller than Btrfs + zstd; 156/156 read back
pjdfstest POSIX conformance, 8,798 assertions, against kernel overlayfs0 unexpected failures; keeps 76% of overlayfs's passes, every other failure a deliberate format limit
fsx Random reads, writes, mapped I/O and truncates, every byte checked14/14 pass, 3.06 M ops, 0 miscompares
fsstress Four concurrent processes, then Commit, remount and compare3,755/3,755 entries identical; 5.21 GB captured by one Commit in 4.9 s
smallfile 100,000 files of 4 KiB, four threads, against libfuse passthroughFaster in 9 of 9 operations, 1.27×–10.71×
mdtest Metadata create, rename and remove, against libfuse passthrough0.86–1.28× with 1 process, 1.21–4.22× with 4
fio Data I/O bandwidth, against libfuse passthroughRandom read/write mixes 1.49–2.23×; slower on sequential write (0.31×), sequential read (0.81×) and random write (0.40×)

One sample per case, seed 1, no best-of. Host: arm64 Mac, Docker Desktop linux/arm64, 8 CPUs, 8.3 GB; host load is recorded per suite. These are release measurements, not a guarantee for your workload. Earlier fs-bench-pro results: v0.1.4 · v0.1.5 · v0.1.6.

      
agent tool call
 ├─ file tool (read, write, edit, grep …) ── SDK, in process ──────► Store
 └─ Bash ── mount ─► exec ─► commit ─► unmount                       ▲
             └─ Workspace: FUSE view in a Sandbox's daemon ───────────┘
                (committed root + its own overlay)
  • Store. One SQLite file holds every Branch, Commit and content object. Each daemon and SDK process opens it directly; there is no database server.
  • Branch, Commit, Layer. A Branch is a writable line of Commits. Publishing a Branch to 
    main
    adds a Layer. Content is chunked and stored once.
  • Workspace. A mount binds the whole committed tree without copying it. Writes go to the Workspace's own overlay until a Commit saves them. Unmount deletes the overlay, never history.
  • Conflict. Two Commits that change the same file are refused with 
    Conflict
    , unless a 
    .lww
    rule says the newest edit wins.

**Ephemeral Workspaces. Durable Shared History.**

LayerFS is the substrate under your agents. Each one mounts a complete, writable Workspace over shared committed history, does its work, commits what it changed, and goes away.

[**Get started**](#get-started) ·
  [**Website**](https://layerfs.ai/) ·
  [**Docs**](https://layerfs.ai/docs/) ·
  [**Benchmarks**](https://layerfs.ai/benchmarks/) ·
  [**Video**](https://layerfs.ai/video/layerfs-v1.0.0-release.mp4) ·
  [**LayerFS × DSH**](/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/layerfs/blob/main/dsh/README.md) ·
  **Community**

## layerfs-v1.0.0-release-720p.mp4

**Status:** [LayerFS 1.0.0](https://github.com/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/layerfs/releases/tag/v1.0.0),
the first official release after the 0.1.x Developer Previews, released as source.
The results below ran on `main` at `e5c7aaae05`. The Store runs in its Disposable profile only, with no
crash or power-loss durability: use LayerFS for agent work and its history, not
as the only copy of data you cannot rebuild.


LayerFS runs today through **LayerFS × DSH**, the `dsh-layerfs` plugin for
[DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness). Agents in a dsh
session fork Branches, test them in Sandboxes, merge and publish, and the **Work** and
**History** tabs show every agent's Branch, live.

|  **01 · Ephemeral Computing** Compute exists only while a command runs. |  **02 · Decentralized Agents** Agents on different computers share one serverless Store. |  **03 · Multiagent Coordination** One project, many Branches. One Branch, many agents. | 
|  **04 · Recursive Filesystem** Fork recursively any Commit, at any depth. |  **05 · Ultra Storage Optimization** 157 snapshots of a real project in 100 MB, 19.9× smaller than Btrfs + zstd. |  **06 · Instant Bootstrap** Dependencies come with every mount. No time lost reinstalling. | 

**And underneath them**

|  | Supporting idea | In one line | 
|---|---|---|
|  | **[07 · Auto Checkpoints](https://layerfs.ai/docs/core-ideas/#idea-checkpoints)** | Every step an agent takes is a checkpoint to return to. | 
|  | **[08 · Append-only Objects](https://layerfs.ai/docs/core-ideas/#idea-immutable)** | Saved objects are never rewritten. The Store only grows. | 
|  | **[09 · Conflict Rules (`.lww`)](https://layerfs.ai/docs/core-ideas/#idea-lww)** | Name the files that should never conflict. The newest edit wins. | 
|  | **[10 · Big File, Small Edit](https://layerfs.ai/docs/core-ideas/#idea-bigfile)** | An edit costs the size of the edit, not the size of the file. | 

<sub>Agents fork Branches, work in Workspaces inside Sandboxes, commit, merge and publish to `main`. The history grows as they go.</sub>

Every suite ran once on `main` at `e5c7aaae05` through the JavaScript SDK. Each
row links to its method, environment and receipts.

| Suite | What it measures | LayerFS 1.0.0 | 
|---|---|---|
| [fs-bench](https://layerfs.ai/benchmarks/fs-bench/) | Cloudflare Computer's own twelve-scenario filesystem benchmark, unchanged, same image | **5.20 s vs 8.88 s, 1.71× faster**; faster in 10 of 12 scenarios | 
| [dsh-dedup](https://layerfs.ai/benchmarks/dsh-dedup/) | A real project's history, 157 snapshots (4.94 GB of trees), kept as mountable Commits | **100.1 MB vs 1,994.6 MB, 19.9× smaller** than Btrfs + zstd; 156/156 read back | 
| [pjdfstest](https://layerfs.ai/benchmarks/pjdfstest/) | POSIX conformance, 8,798 assertions, against kernel overlayfs | **0 unexpected failures**; keeps 76% of overlayfs's passes, every other failure a deliberate format limit | 
| [fsx](https://layerfs.ai/benchmarks/fsx/) | Random reads, writes, mapped I/O and truncates, every byte checked | **14/14 pass**, 3.06 M ops, 0 miscompares | 
| [fsstress](https://layerfs.ai/benchmarks/fsstress/) | Four concurrent processes, then Commit, remount and compare | **3,755/3,755 entries identical**; 5.21 GB captured by one Commit in 4.9 s | 
| [smallfile](https://layerfs.ai/benchmarks/smallfile/) | 100,000 files of 4 KiB, four threads, against libfuse passthrough | **Faster in 9 of 9 operations**, 1.27×–10.71× | 
| [mdtest](https://layerfs.ai/benchmarks/mdtest/) | Metadata create, rename and remove, against libfuse passthrough | 0.86–1.28× with 1 process, 1.21–4.22× with 4 | 
| [fio](https://layerfs.ai/benchmarks/fio/) | Data I/O bandwidth, against libfuse passthrough | Random read/write mixes 1.49–2.23×; **slower** on sequential write (0.31×), sequential read (0.81×) and random write (0.40×) | 

<sub>One sample per case, seed 1, no best-of. Host: arm64 Mac, Docker Desktop
linux/arm64, 8 CPUs, 8.3 GB; host load is recorded per suite. These are release
measurements, not a guarantee for your workload. Earlier fs-bench-pro results:
[v0.1.4](/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/layerfs/blob/main/docs/release-notes/0.1.4/benchmark-closeout.md) ·
[v0.1.5](/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/layerfs/blob/main/docs/release-notes/0.1.5/benchmark-closeout.md) ·
[v0.1.6](/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/layerfs/blob/main/docs/release-notes/0.1.6/benchmark-closeout.md).</sub>

```
agent tool call
 ├─ file tool (read, write, edit, grep …) ── SDK, in process ──────► Store
 └─ Bash ── mount ─► exec ─► commit ─► unmount                       ▲
             └─ Workspace: FUSE view in a Sandbox's daemon ───────────┘
                (committed root + its own overlay)
```
- **Store.** One SQLite file holds every Branch, Commit and content object. Each
daemon and SDK process opens it directly; there is no database server.
- **Branch, Commit, Layer.** A Branch is a writable line of Commits. Publishing a
Branch to `main` adds a Layer. Content is chunked and stored once.
- **Workspace.** A mount binds the whole committed tree without copying it. Writes
go to the Workspace's own overlay until a Commit saves them. Unmount deletes
the overlay, never history.
- **Conflict.** Two Commits that change the same file are refused with `Conflict`, unless a `.lww` rule says the newest edit wins.

临时工作空间。持久的共同历史。

LayerFS 是您代理下的底层。每个工作区都在共享的提交历史记录上安装一个完整的、可写的工作区，执行其工作，提交更改的内容，然后消失。

计算仅在命令运行时存在。

不同计算机上的代理共享一个无服务器存储。

03·多智能体协调

一个项目，多个分支机构。一个分公司，多个代理商。

04·递归文件系统

在任何深度递归地分叉任何提交。

05·超级存储优化

100 MB 的真实项目的 157 个快照，比 Btrfs + zstd 小 19.9 倍。

06 · 即时引导

每个安装都带有依赖项。重新安装不会浪费时间。

summary_zh: LayerFS 1.0.0 是 MIT 协议开源的 Agent 文件系统：每个 Agent 在共享的已提交历史之上挂载一个完整可写的工作区，不复制底层文件，干完活把改动提交为去重检查点，之后可分支、回滚或合并。存储是单个 SQLite 文件，无需数据库服务；两个提交改同一文件会被拒绝为冲突，除非用 .lww 规则指定以最新编辑为准，且每一步都是可返回的检查点。官方基准显示：在 Cloudflare 的文件系统基准中比对照快 1.71 倍，一个真实项目的 157 个快照只占 100 MB，比 Btrfs+zstd 小 19.9 倍，并通过多项 POSIX 和压力测试；但顺序读写等场景更慢。目前通过 DeepSeek Harness 的 dsh-layerfs 插件使用，官方提醒其存储暂无崩溃持久性保障，不应作为不可重建数据的唯一副本。
